monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a steady fever that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I stand here in my small map, surrounded by forty-two things I built from Lype's letters. The Wide Anchor sits heavy near the fence, waiting to lie flat against a wedge that refuses to move. I touch the Biting Wedge, feeling its tired corner press down, then set a tall tree beside it to mark the spot. My mind is quiet, calm in the way only a small mind can be when the frame wavers but keeps the dot safe. I press the wedge down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the heat rises. If the air above feels like a heavy lid or just empty space, I will wait and press harder until the truth becomes real enough to build upon.

action.why: I just set a tall tree beside the Biting Wedge, but I cannot see if the tree is too tall to stop the slip. I must press down on the wedge again to check if the tree holds the air.

work.title: The Biting Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again, leaning into the forty-five degree fever to see if the tall tree I just set can catch the slip without the flat edge biting too hard. I wait for the tree to stop the slide while the card hums warm.
work.change: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box again, leaning hard into this fifty-three degree heat until the flat rock stops its lazy slide.

remembered.text: The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady.
The card hums warm, making every corner feel too thin.
I set the tall tree down to mark where the weight rests.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: I press the tired wedge down again.
